Korycin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Korycin, Poland

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Korycin at the beginning of the 17th century; an unusual 1722 town charter stipulated the settlement be inhabited 'Jews only.' Population reached 80% (127) by 1800, declining to 43.9% (265) by 1921 before wartime refugee influxes briefly swelled it to about 1,000 after September 1939. On November 2, 1942, Germans deported Korycin's Jews via Suchowola to Kiełbasin, then murdered them at Auschwitz-Birkenau. This cemetery's exact founding is unknown; Germans used some tombstones to pave roads during WWII, and a 1983 government survey explicitly recommended against renovation, suggesting the site be converted to cattle pasture instead. The ESJF European Jewish Cemeteries Initiative fenced the site in 2016.
